extracted.intended_audience: general readers; youths considering apprenticeship, farming, or practical education
extracted.subtask_description: First‑person memoir recounting rural childhood, farm labor, and an apprenticeship in a 19th‑century printing office, with reflective advice about education, apprenticeship organization, and farming as a vocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: an_apprentice_should_have_one_master
rubrics_metrics.description: “an apprentice should have one master; while I had a series of them, and often two or three at once.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as a normative organizational rule for apprenticeships: having multiple successive masters is described as 'vicious' because it undermines consistent instruction. Example/anti-pattern: the author's office passed through several owners and managers (editors, printers, a mercantile firm), producing lax rule and inconsistent oversight. Implied recommendation: appoint a single master to ensure steady, coherent training.

rubrics_metrics.name: learn_a_trade_of_a_good_master
rubrics_metrics.description: “To the youth who asks, 'How shall I obtain an education?' I would answer, 'Learn a trade of a good master.' I hold firmly that most boys may thus better acquire the knowledge they need than by spending four years in college.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit adult advice for youths: vocational apprenticeship under a competent master is recommended as a superior means for many young people to gain practical knowledge compared with a traditional four‑year college. Supporting remarks note access to books, public library, and practical on‑the‑job learning during apprenticeship. Implied evaluation criterion for education routes: practicality and direct skill acquisition are valued over formal degree time.

rubrics_metrics.name: rural_common_schools_teach_practical_sciences_not_advanced_algebra
rubrics_metrics.description: “I deeply regret that such homely sciences as Chemistry, Geology, and Botany were never taught, — were not even named therein. ... Yet, I am thankful that Algebra had not yet been thrust into our rural common schools, to knot the brains and squander the time of those who should be learning something of positive and practical utility.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prescription for rural school curricula: prioritize practical natural sciences (chemistry, geology, botany) that offer positive, practical utility to rural students; avoid introducing abstract topics (exemplified by advanced algebra) too early if they divert time from practically useful learning. This functions as a content‑selection criterion for rural education.

rubrics_metrics.name: farming_should_be_ennobling_intellectual_pursuit
rubrics_metrics.description: “Our farmers' sons escape from their fathers' calling whenever they can, because it is made a mindless, monotonous drudgery, instead of an ennobling, liberalizing, intellectual pursuit.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normative standard for the practice and training of agriculture: farming ought to provide scope for expanding faculties, continual growth in knowledge, and incentive for ambition; when it is reduced to unthinking drudgery, sons abandon it. Implied recommendation: agricultural training should be intellectual and liberalizing to retain successors and produce efficient farmers.

rubrics_metrics.name: apprenticeship_contract_terms_should_be_explicit
rubrics_metrics.description: Narrative example: the author was to 'remain till twenty years of age, be allowed my board only for six months, and thereafter $40 per annum in addition for my clothing.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit criterion for apprenticeship agreements: contracts should clearly state duration, provision for board, and allowances or wages. The narration shows concrete terms and also illustrates that changes in ownership/management can alter conditions (leading to eventual demand for more liberal allowance). Anti-pattern: vague or changing terms may enable exploitation or later disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: apprentice_conduct_diligence_and_temperance
rubrics_metrics.description: “I worked diligently... I never fished, nor hunted, nor attended a dance, nor any sort of party or fandango... I doubt that I even played a game of ball.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Behavioral guidance for apprentices: steady, faithful work, avoidance of dissipations and social distractions, and use of leisure for reading and self‑improvement are portrayed as virtues that earn trust and instructional opportunities from superiors. Positive outcome: access to books, public library, and substantial learning despite hard labor. Implied evaluation: apprentices should be judged by industriousness and self‑directed study.
